As primary season continues, some Democrats claim the party needs to "move to the center" to win in November.

Hogwash.

Democrats can't repeat the same failed playbook of the last 50 years. It's time for them to grow a spine.

Video

While corporate profits skyrocket and the stock market rides high, regular Americans are struggling to make ends meet.

Even CEOs of the biggest corporations are starting to understand why this is a huge problem. Watch.

Video

The NRA buys off Congress. No action on guns.

The oil industry buys off Congress. No action on climate.

Insurance companies buy off Congress. No action on health care.

The list goes on and on.

Money in politics is the root of our dysfunction.

For years, Hungary's Viktor Orban gerrymandered his opposition out of power.

But in the end, all the dirty tricks in the world couldn't save him from sinking approval ratings and massive voter turnout.

There's a lesson here for us.

Video

Will the new Southern gerrymanders be enough for the GOP to hold the House?

Will they pass another Big Ugly Bill before November?

Is the Iran War ever going to end?

Michael and I answer the week's burning questions on today's Klatch. piped.video/iSr0jy-oeGg

In 2023, Justin Jones was expelled from the Tennessee House for standing up for democracy.

Today, he's back in office and fighting the good fight against the GOP's racist power-grab.

I was honored to chat with him a few years back. piped.video/watch?v=lyvpDPuG…

Trump's DOJ just ended a major Biden-era antitrust lawsuit against AgriStats — whose price-fixing scheme allegedly raised chicken, pork, and turkey prices — with a slap-on-the-wrist settlement.

Amid rising inflation, Trump has given Big Ag the green light to rip you off more. commondreams.org/news/trump-…

The most powerful force in American politics today is anti-establishment fury at a rigged economic system.

To counter Trump’s culture wars and fake populism, progressives must mount a real battle against economic elites who have rigged the game — and shafted millions of working class people.

Who represents the future of the Democratic Party?

Hint: It's not Chuck Schumer or Rahm Emanuel.

Some thoughts...

robertreich.substack.com/p/h…

Reminder...

Any political party trying to make it harder to vote is sending a clear message — they can't win on their ideas alone.

Remember: Wealth cannot be separated from power.

We're seeing in real time how the extreme concentration of wealth is distorting our politics, rigging markets, and granting unprecedented power to a handful of people.

Taxing the rich isn't just an economic issue, it's a defense of our democracy.

Alito flew multiple flags tied to Jan 6 insurrectionists.

Thomas just gave a speech on how "progressivism" is destroying the country — plus his wife was involved in the Jan 6 plot.

And Roberts has pushed "shadow docket" cases where justices make decisions without explaining themselves.


Lawrence Hurley (@lawrencehurley)

NEW: Chief Justice John Roberts bemoans that Americans don't understand how the Supreme Court operates and see justices as "political actors". The court at times simply has t

Friends — We are witnessing what happens to a person who is consumed with the need to dominate but cannot.

Trump's looming failure in Iran is not just a serious geopolitical defeat for the United States; it’s a personal crisis.

Be warned. robertreich.substack.com/p/t…

Our media is controlled by just a handful of billionaires and their corporations. And Trump is making things even worse.

Here's how we stop it.

Video

The corporate takeover of American politics was rapid and ruthless.

In the 1970s, I watched as thousands of corporate lobbyists descended on Washington. Fast forward to today, and lobbying has become a multi-billion dollar industry.

It all began with the Powell Memo.

Video

Billionaire tax cuts are a policy choice.

Cutting healthcare for millions is a policy choice.

Cutting food assistance for children is a policy choice.

Taking from the poor and giving to the rich is a policy choice.

It does not have to be like this.

In another Dem overperformance last night, Democrat Chedrick Greene won by 9 points in a MI Senate seat Kamala Harris barely won.

Dems will retain control of the chamber through 2026.

The midterm momentum is against Trump and the GOP — which is why they're fighting to rig maps.

As primary season continues, some Democrats claim the party needs to "move to the center" to win in November.

Hogwash.

Democrats can't repeat the same failed playbook of the last 50 years. It's time for them to grow a spine. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EQzG_TrhyrY

I have been a vocal critic of gerrymandering.

But the Supreme Court has unleashed the Republican Party on a gerrymandering spree.

Democrats must respond in kind, removing any incentive for Republican states to gerrymander.

This isn’t a race to the bottom. It’s a means of avoiding the bottom.

Between the VA ruling and the TN power-grab, the GOP seems to be winning the gerrymandering war.

But will it be enough to defend their House majority under an unpopular president and surging inflation?

Let's discuss on this week's Coffee Klatch.

Even CEOs of the biggest corporations are starting to understand why this is a huge problem. Watch. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W8OWhw-GXUU

The NRA buys off Congress. No action on guns.

The oil industry buys off Congress. No action on climate.

Insurance companies buy off Congress. No action on health care.

The list goes on and on.

Money in politics is the root of our dysfunction.

For years, Hungary's Viktor Orban gerrymandered his opposition out of power.

But in the end, all the dirty tricks in the world couldn't save him from sinking approval ratings and massive voter turnout.

There's a lesson here for us.

Will the new Southern gerrymanders be enough for the GOP to hold the House?

Will they pass another Big Ugly Bill before November?

Is the Iran War ever going to end?

Michael and I answer the week's burning questions on today's Klatch.

94% of teachers have to dip into their own pockets to buy school supplies.

85% of teachers are working second jobs during the school year, often just to keep up with the cost of living.

Meanwhile, the average Wall Street employee got a bonus of $246,900 in 2025.

Something has gone terribly wrong.

Giving billionaires and corporations the green light to buy our elections.

Making it easier for polluters to destroy the planet.

Stripping millions of reproductive freedom.

Granting presidents immunity.

Gutting the protections of the Voting Rights Act.

The shame of the John Roberts court.

In 2023, Justin Jones was expelled from the Tennessee House for standing up for democracy.

Today, he's back in office and fighting the good fight against the GOP's racist power-grab.

I was honored to chat with him a few years back. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lyvpDPuGxdU

Crippling our ability to anticipate & track storms & then also crippling our ability to aid communities hit by storms & then also crippling any kind of social safety net that might help individuals hurt by storms. 

The GOP is a death cult. It's not a metaphor.

Trump's DOJ just ended a major Biden-era antitrust lawsuit against AgriStats — whose price-fixing scheme allegedly raised chicken, pork, and turkey prices — with a slap-on-the-wrist settlement.

Amid rising inflation, Trump has given Big Ag the green light to rip you off more.

Trump slashed funding for researching infectious diseases like hantavirus and made deep staffing cuts to the CDC and other agencies that coordinate outbreak response.

His disastrous decision-making cost us during the last pandemic — and continues to put us in danger. www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/h...

The most powerful force in American politics today is anti-establishment fury at a rigged economic system.

To counter Trump’s culture wars and fake populism, progressives must mount a real battle against economic elites who have rigged the game — and shafted millions of working class people.

Who represents the future of the Democratic Party?

Hint: It's not Chuck Schumer or Rahm Emanuel.

Some thoughts...

https://robertreich.substack.com/p/heres-how-democrats-are-responding

Reminder...

Any political party trying to make it harder to vote is sending a clear message — they can't win on their ideas alone.

So, SCOTUS says Red states can ignore the will of the people and gerrymander their districts 9-0 in favor of MAGA

But VA Supreme Court says Blue states cannot put the vote to the will of the people and follow through on the people's will to redistrict.

Beyond Absurd.

2/2
How the fuck does the GOP explain this? www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/...
The rules of redistricting are simple: Republicans are free to do whatever they want, and Democrats are also free to do whatever Republicans want.

Wow. Chaos on the Tennessee House floor. Tennesseans yelling in the gallery and Democrats locking arms in one final stand, as Republicans vote to advance new congressional maps that will carve up the state’s only majority-Black congressional district.

For years, Hungary's Viktor Orban gerrymandered his opposition out of power. But in the end, all the dirty tricks in the world couldn't save him from sinking approval ratings and massive voter turnout. There's a lesson here for us.
Our media is controlled by just a handful of billionaires and their corporations. And Trump is making things even worse. Here's how we stop it.
This week is Teacher Appreciation Week. Let me tell you about one teacher in particular who changed my life forever. Mrs. Alice Camp.
The greatest honor of my life wasn't serving in the Cabinet. It was being a teacher.
I've spent a lifetime teaching young people — and I wouldn't trade it for anything in the world. These are the most important lessons I've learned along the way.
Trump's tariffs and war with Iran are costing the American people more every day. In November, the GOP will pay the price.
Why is the President of the United States shilling so hard for cryptocurrency? Because the entire industry is a Ponzi scheme — and he's the conman-in-chief.

The Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act of 1965 this week. It was a slap in the face to the countless activists who fought for the VRA — and those who died for it. But we cannot give up. Here's how we should respond.
You've probably heard a lot about general strikes. But how exactly do they work? And is America on the verge of one? Labor journalist Kim Kelly explains.
The decision made today by the Supreme Court’s conservative majority was dishonest and shameful. I want to share some thoughts on what it means — and how we move forward.
